sections.reason: Title block, Status of this Memo, copyright notice, Abstract and table of contents.
Introduction. States the purpose of the six attributes; no normative keyword.
Attributes. Introduces the six attribute sections; no keyword of its own.
NAS-IPv6-Address. One MUST (NAS-Identifier when neither address is present), one SHOULD on uniqueness and one MAY on presence, all captured.
Framed-Interface-Id, printed as 3.2 in the RFC where 2.2 was meant. One conditional MUST captured as RFC3162-3.2-1 and one MAY captured as RFC3162-3.2-2.
Framed-IPv6-Prefix. The Reserved-field MUST and two MAYs are captured.
Login-IPv6-Host. Two MAYs; the request hint is captured as RFC3162-2.4-1. No MUST.
Framed-IPv6-Route. The text MUST NOT and the SHOULD on an unspecified gateway are captured; the text format SHOULD is described in the summary.
Framed-IPv6-Pool. The MUST to ignore and the SHOULD to use the pool are captured.
Table of Attributes. The quantity table is reproduced in the summary; it carries no legend with keywords.
Security Considerations. The zero-length secret MUST is captured as RFC3162-5-1.
Authors' Addresses and the full copyright statement.

sites.quote: NAS-IPv6- Address and/or NAS-IP-Address MAY be present in an Access-Request packet; however, if neither attribute is present then NAS- Identifier MUST be present.

If the Interface-Identifier IPv6CP option [11] has been successfully negotiated, this Attribute MUST be included in an Access-Request packet as a hint by the NAS to the server that it would prefer that value.
This field, which is reserved and MUST be present, is always set to zero.
It is intended to be human readable and MUST NOT affect operation of the protocol.
If a NAS does not support multiple prefix pools, the NAS MUST ignore this Attribute.
In this case, a shared secret of zero length MUST be assumed.
